mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.4% indicates an easing monetary policy, which reduces the risk-free rate and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.4%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% signals accelerating inflation, which typically triggers a monetary policy tightening by the Fed, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher interest rates.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 3-month moving averages indicates strong economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates continued economic growth and corporate earnings expansion.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST are above their 3-month moving averages, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.5%), the labor market is tight, which typically leads to higher wage growth and inflationary pressures, causing the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) above 1.0% signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the weakening economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO falls > 1.0% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 2.0% signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates a slowdown in economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS falls > 2.0% year-over-year, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% year-over-year signals a tightening monetary policy cycle amid rising inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 2.0% year-over-year, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 0.5% signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS falls > 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
